passages.text: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to entrust with my sheep dogs.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is an older man.
Younger men now mock Job.
These men are younger than Job.
Job would not have trusted their fathers.
Job would not have let their fathers care for his sheep dogs.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֤ה׀ שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים מִמֶּ֗נִּי לְיָ֫מִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ מָאַ֥סְתִּי אֲבוֹתָ֑ם לָ֝שִׁ֗ית עִם־ כַּלְבֵ֥י צֹאנִֽי׃

passages.text: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job refers to men who are younger than he is.
These men mock Job.
Job says their fathers were weak and useless to him.
Job asks, “Why would I need the strength of their hands?”
Job explains that their strength is gone.
Their vigor has left them.
Their hands are of no use to Job.
passages.original: גַּם־ כֹּ֣חַ יְ֭דֵיהֶם לָ֣מָּה לִּ֑י עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ אָ֣בַד כָּֽלַח׃

passages.text: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.
passages.sermon:
These people suffered from poverty.
They also suffered from hunger.
They became thin and gaunt.
They wandered in the dry land.
They searched for food in the wilderness.
At night, they lived in the desolate wasteland.
passages.original: בְּחֶ֥סֶר וּבְכָפָ֗ן גַּ֫לְמ֥וּד הַֽעֹרְקִ֥ים צִיָּ֑ה אֶ֝֗מֶשׁ שׁוֹאָ֥ה וּמְשֹׁאָֽה׃

passages.text: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.
passages.sermon:
These people were poor and hungry.
They searched for food among the shrubs.
They picked mallow leaves to eat.
They dug up roots from the broom tree.
They ate these roots as their food.
passages.original: הַקֹּטְפִ֣ים מַלּ֣וּחַ עֲלֵי־ שִׂ֑יחַ וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ רְתָמִ֣ים לַחְמָֽם׃

passages.text: They were banished from among men, shouted down like thieves, so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
passages.sermon:
These people were outcasts.
Other people drove them away.
People shouted at them like they were thieves.
They could not live with others.
They lived on the slopes of dry riverbeds.
They made their homes among the rocks.
They hid in holes in the ground.
passages.original: מִן־ גֵּ֥ו יְגֹרָ֑שׁוּ יָרִ֥יעוּ עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ כַּגַּנָּֽב׃ בַּעֲר֣וּץ נְחָלִ֣ים לִשְׁכֹּ֑ן חֹרֵ֖י עָפָ֣ר וְכֵפִֽים׃

passages.text: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.
passages.sermon:
These people lived in great hardship.
They cried out among the shrubs.
They huddled beneath the nettles.
They suffered and found shelter only in wild, rough places.
passages.original: בֵּין־ שִׂיחִ֥ים יִנְהָ֑קוּ תַּ֖חַת חָר֣וּל יְסֻפָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.
passages.sermon:
These people are sons of fools.
They are sons of those with no name.
They have no honor.
People drove them out from the land.
passages.original: בְּֽנֵי־ נָ֭בָל גַּם־ בְּנֵ֣י בְלִי־ שֵׁ֑ם נִ֝כְּא֗וּ מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
People now mock Job in their songs.
They use Job’s name as a byword.
They speak about Job with scorn.
passages.original: וְ֭עַתָּה נְגִינָתָ֣ם הָיִ֑יתִי וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
passages.sermon: The people hate me.\r\nThey stay far away from me.\r\nThey do not hold back from spitting in my face.
passages.original: תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי רָ֣חֲקוּ מֶ֑נִּי וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י לֹא־ חָ֥שְׂכוּ רֹֽק׃

passages.text: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
passages.sermon:
God has taken away my strength.
God has caused me to suffer.
People see that God has done this to me.
They no longer control themselves around me.
They act without restraint in front of me.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִתְרוֹ פִ֭תַּח וַיְעַנֵּ֑נִי וְ֝רֶ֗סֶן מִפָּנַ֥י שִׁלֵּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is suffering greatly.
People who have no status or respect rise up at Job’s right side.
These people are called the rabble.
They attack Job.
They set traps for Job’s feet.
They try to make Job stumble.
They build siege ramps against Job.
They prepare to harm Job.
They act as enemies surrounding Job.
passages.original: עַל־ יָמִין֮ פִּרְחַ֪ח יָ֫ק֥וּמוּ רַגְלַ֥י שִׁלֵּ֑חוּ וַיָּסֹ֥לּוּ עָ֝לַ֗י אָרְח֥וֹת אֵידָֽם׃

passages.text: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.
passages.sermon:
My enemies tear up my path.
They seek to harm me.
They gain from my destruction.
No one stops them.
No one helps me.
passages.original: נָתְס֗וּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י לְהַוָּתִ֥י יֹעִ֑ילוּ לֹ֖א עֹזֵ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in.
passages.sermon:
My enemies attack me.
They come forward like soldiers entering a wide gap in a wall.
They move through the ruins.
They keep coming in without stopping.
passages.original: כְּפֶ֣רֶץ רָחָ֣ב יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ תַּ֥חַת שֹׁ֝אָ֗ה הִתְגַּלְגָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job suffers greatly.
Terrors attack Job.
Terrors come against Job.
Terrors overwhelm Job.
Terrors chase away Job’s dignity.
The wind blows away Job’s dignity.
Job’s prosperity disappears.
Job’s prosperity passes quickly.
Job’s prosperity vanishes like a cloud.
passages.original: הָהְפַּ֥ךְ עָלַ֗י בַּלָּ֫ה֥וֹת תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He says his soul is poured out within him.
He feels empty inside.
Days of affliction grip him.
Suffering holds him tightly.
He cannot escape his pain.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי יְמֵי־ עֹֽנִי׃

passages.text: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
Night brings pain to my bones.
My body feels sharp, deep aches.
My pains do not stop.
My suffering never rests.
passages.original: לַ֗יְלָה עֲ֭צָמַי נִקַּ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְ֝עֹרְקַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁכָּבֽוּן׃

passages.text: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
passages.sermon: God acts with great power.\r\nHe grabs my clothing.\r\nHe holds me tightly by the collar of my tunic.
passages.original: בְּרָב־ כֹּ֭חַ יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ לְבוּשִׁ֑י כְּפִ֖י כֻתָּנְתִּ֣י יַֽאַזְרֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
passages.sermon: God throws me into the mud.\r\nI become like dust.\r\nI become like ashes.
passages.original: הֹרָ֥נִי לַחֹ֑מֶר וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל כֶּעָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job cries out to God for help.
God does not answer Job.
Job stands before God.
God only looks at Job.
passages.original: אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי עָ֝מַ֗דְתִּי וַתִּתְבֹּ֥נֶן בִּֽי׃

passages.text: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels abandoned.
God has become cruel to Job.
God uses His strong hand against Job.
God opposes Job with power.
passages.original: תֵּהָפֵ֣ךְ לְאַכְזָ֣ר לִ֑י בְּעֹ֖צֶם יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels powerless.
God takes Job up into the wind.
God drives Job before the wind.
God tosses Job about in the storm.
Job cannot control what happens.
God’s actions overwhelm Job.
passages.original: תִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי אֶל־ ר֭וּחַ תַּרְכִּיבֵ֑נִי וּ֝תְמֹגְגֵ֗נִי תְּשֻׁוֶּה׃

passages.text: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job knows God will bring him down to death.
Death is the place God has appointed for all living people.
All people must go to this place.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יָ֭דַעְתִּי מָ֣וֶת תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי וּבֵ֖ית מוֹעֵ֣ד לְכָל־ חָֽי׃

passages.text: Yet no one stretches out his hand to a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.
passages.sermon:
A ruined man suffers.
He cries for help in his distress.
No one stretches out his hand to him.
No one helps him.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ לֹא־ בְ֭עִי יִשְׁלַח־ יָ֑ד אִם־ בְּ֝פִיד֗וֹ לָהֶ֥ן שֽׁוּעַ׃

passages.text: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
passages.sermon:
I am Job.
I have suffered greatly.
I have wept for people in trouble.
My soul has grieved for the needy.
passages.original: אִם־ לֹ֣א בָ֭כִיתִי לִקְשֵׁה־ י֑וֹם עָֽגְמָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He hoped for good things.
Evil came instead.
He looked for light.
Darkness came instead.
passages.original: כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב קִ֭וִּיתִי וַיָּ֣בֹא רָ֑ע וַֽאֲיַחֲלָ֥ה לְ֝א֗וֹר וַיָּ֥בֹא אֹֽפֶל׃

passages.text: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels deep pain inside.
His heart churns within him.
He cannot find rest.
Days of trouble come to him.
Affliction meets him every day.
passages.original: מֵעַ֖י רֻתְּח֥וּ וְלֹא־ דָ֗מּוּ קִדְּמֻ֥נִי יְמֵי־ עֹֽנִי׃

passages.text: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He feels deep sorrow.
He walks in darkness.
The sun does not cause this darkness.
He stands among people.
He cries out for help.
passages.original: קֹדֵ֣ר הִ֭לַּכְתִּי בְּלֹ֣א חַמָּ֑ה קַ֖מְתִּי בַקָּהָ֣ל אֲשַׁוֵּֽעַ׃

passages.text: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He feels alone and rejected.
He says, “I have become a brother of jackals.”
He also says, “I am a companion of ostriches.”
Jackals are wild and live in desolate places.
Ostriches are lonely and dwell in the wilderness.
Job feels like he belongs with these outcasts.
He feels separated from people.
He feels abandoned and isolated.
passages.original: אָ֭ח הָיִ֣יתִי לְתַנִּ֑ים וְ֝רֵ֗עַ לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃

passages.text: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job suffers greatly.
His skin turns black.
His skin peels away.
His bones burn with fever.
Job feels pain in his body.
passages.original: ע֭וֹרִי שָׁחַ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְעַצְמִי־ חָ֝֗רָה מִנִּי־ חֹֽרֶב׃

passages.text: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job is suffering.
Job says, "My harp plays only sad music."
My harp makes the sound of mourning.
My flute makes the sound of weeping.
My flute does not play joyful music.
My music expresses my grief.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י לְ֭אֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִ֑י וְ֝עֻגָבִ֗י לְק֣וֹל בֹּכִֽים׃
